standard_prerequisites.name: After replacing the ring by a localization at a suitable element, a pseudo-coherent complex splits as the direct sum of its truncation below a degree and its truncation above that degree, the latter being perfect
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the splitting of the complex and the perfectness of the upper truncation.

standard_prerequisites.name: A perfect complex whose fibre over a prime is a finite free complex concentrated in degrees where the dimensions are prescribed can be represented over a suitable localization by the complex with those free modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the perfect object into the displayed bounded complex of free modules with the prescribed ranks.

core_obligations: Enlarge the bound a if necessary so that the cohomology of the complex itself, not only of its fibre, vanishes below a; this does not change the hypothesis (proof lines 20019-20020).

Apply the cutting statement after localizing at a suitable element outside the prime: this splits the complex into the truncation below a minus one and the truncation from a on, with the latter perfect (proof lines 20020-20024).
Since the cohomology below a vanishes, the low truncation is zero in the derived category, so the complex is perfect (proof lines 20024-20026).

Apply the lifting statement to the now perfect object to represent it, after a further localization, by the finite free complex displayed in the statement with the prescribed ranks, which also gives the perfectness conclusion (proof lines 20027-20029).
proof_roadmap: Shift the bound so that the complex vanishes below it (proof lines 20019-20020).
Split off the low truncation locally and see it is zero, so the complex becomes perfect (proof lines 20020-20026).
Represent that perfect object by the displayed finite free complex with the prescribed ranks (proof lines 20027-20029).
